summary: Audited all five remaining control-matching concerns against the code. Verdicts: (1) Per-arm z standardization is a disclosed, necessary, capacity-neutral matching step, not a confound — raw code energy differs 163x between arms (0.098 vs 15.98 mean-square per dim), so standardizing each arm's own code is what makes them comparable, and it is a diagonal affine the first Linear layer can absorb exactly. The observation normalizers are frozen (double-guarded) and are literally the same object across all arms. (2) No clip identity reaches the actor. PROPRIO_SLICE(0,90) is actions+base_ang_vel+dof_pos+dof_vel; GOAL_SLICE(90,154) is motion_command(58)+motion_ref_ori_b(6); motion_id only routes teacher labels and tags reports. The unit test's claim holds in the trainer, and I found a stronger fact the test does not cover: because E70 runs E52_DET=1 the posterior is never called, so critic_obs (the privileged group, which does carry extra reference terms) never reaches the student at all. (3) Evaluation resets are exactly matched — the bodyfix patch overwrites holosoma's noisy reset with the exact reference state, all arms use seed 404, the start grid is a deterministic linspace, the ambiguity grid comes from one SHA-256-gated file, and the trainer asserts the grid was realized. Training-time phase sampling is adaptive per arm: a disclosed upstream choice whose direction is self-correcting, so it cannot manufacture the gap. (4) The advisor's premise is right and the collapse-to-0.000 reading is over-claimed, but the mechanism is narrower than stated: destroy_command_code does remove the encoder's proprio-derived features, yet raw proprio still reaches the decoder directly, so proprioceptive information is not removed — only the encoder's learned summary of it. The load-bearing half of "every bit of competence flows through it" is a structural fact provable from the architecture without any experiment (decoder in_features = 154 = proprio 90 + z_cmd 64); the destruction experiment adds only that the decoder has no trained proprio-only fallback. All three modes are off-manifold. Crucially, E77's already-frozen dose-response supports the advisor: holding z_cmd for 0.1 s drops the explicit student from 0.926 to 0.223, which a slow motion-semantics command should tolerate. (5) I quantified the shuffled arm's identity content: linearly-decodable between-clip mean separation is 8.042 standardized units, identical to the real SNMR latent, versus exactly 0.000 for the clock. Identity was maximally available and bought nothing (0.5524 vs the identity-free clock's 0.5622). Real but weak evidence against map inversion — identity was encoded, not labelled, and the arm was never optimized to invert it. A proper clip-ID+phase arm needs new training code; eval_e71_command_swap.py cannot supply it (frozen-student evaluator, arms hard-restricted, checkpoint hashes pinned). Net: no concern threatens the primary snmr-minus-time contrast (+0.191 [0.124, 0.274]). One reading must be softened (E75), one diagnostic is genuinely still missing.

findings.claim: Per-arm z_mean/z_std is a matching step, not a confound. The clock arm IS normalized by its own statistics, and the raw scales differ so much that not doing so would be the defect.
findings.evidence: scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:236-250 — phase_only/shuffle_latent replace `latents` BEFORE line 250 computes `z_mean, z_std = latents.mean(0), latents.std(0)+1e-6`; z_window() (252-254) standardizes both offsets. Measured on the frozen E70 motions: raw mean-square per dim 0.098 (SNMR latent) vs 15.98 (time code), a 163x energy gap; per-dim std spread 39.5:1 vs 1.9:1; post-standardization effective rank 11.3 vs 28.0.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED (disclosed design choice, not a defect)
findings.consequence: Without per-arm standardization the clock arm would hit z_proj with ~13x larger RMS inputs — an unambiguous mismatch. With it, both arms deliver a zero-mean unit-variance 256-d vector to an identical z_proj. Standardization is an invertible diagonal affine map, so z_proj's first Linear (256->256) can represent its exact inverse: it cannot change representational capacity, only initialization conditioning, and cannot account for 0.754 vs 0.562.

findings.claim: Per-dim standardization neither smuggles in nor destroys clip identity, because the statistics are pool-wide, not per-clip.
findings.evidence: scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:250 computes statistics over the full concatenated two-clip tensor. Measured between-clip mean separation after standardization: SNMR 8.042 std units, shuffled 8.042, time exactly 0.000.
findings.consequence: Closes the residual form of the normalization concern: the hypothesis that 'each arm's normalizer encodes which clip you are in' is false — statistics are clip-independent by construction and the measured clip separation is preserved, not created.

findings.claim: actor_norm and critic_norm are frozen, double-guarded against updating, and are the SAME object across every arm.
findings.evidence: scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:162-179 — `actor_norm = teacher_actor_norms[0]` (first specialist's normalizer from its checkpoint), `.eval()` at 165/176, `requires_grad_(False)` at 177-179; split_obs (274-278) calls both with `update=False`. holosoma's EmpiricalNormalization.forward gates updates on `if self.training and update` (src/holosoma/holosoma/agents/ppo/ppo.py:58), so either guard alone suffices. Lines 169-171 state the intent: 'Student inputs use one shared normalization (the first specialist), so normalizer statistics cannot serve as a per-motion identifier.'
findings.consequence: Does not threaten any conclusion. Observation normalization is bit-identical across arms and across clips within an arm, and deterministically reproducible from the manifest. The only residual is that clip 2's observations are centered with clip 1's statistics — a shared, disclosed mis-centering hitting all five arms equally.

findings.claim: Nothing in the actor-visible observation carries clip identity as a label; both slices trace to purely state- or reference-valued terms.
findings.evidence: holosoma concatenates observation terms alphabetically (src/holosoma/holosoma/managers/observation/manager.py:139-142, `sorted(obs_tensors.keys())`). For g1_29dof_wbt_observation (src/holosoma/holosoma/config_values/wbt/g1/observation.py:5-39) the actor terms sort to actions(29)|base_ang_vel(3)|dof_pos(29)|dof_vel(29)|motion_command(58)|motion_ref_ori_b(6)=154, matching the assert at scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:139. motion_command is `cat(joint_pos, joint_vel)` of the reference at time_steps (managers/command/terms/wbt.py:827-828); motion_ref_ori_b is a 6-d relative orientation (managers/observation/terms/wbt.py:149-158).
findings.consequence: No index, no one-hot, no clip-conditional scaling. The honest caveat is different and sharper: the explicit arm's 58-d reference joint_pos+joint_vel is, on deterministic clips, a near-unique fingerprint of (clip, frame). That is not a leak — it is the explicit reference the arm is defined to receive — but it means the explicit-vs-latent gap is itself not free of the memorization reading, which is exactly what E71 was designed to settle.

findings.claim: The unit test's claim holds in the trainer, not just in the test: motion_id routes teacher labels and tags reports, and enters no student input path.
findings.evidence: tests/test_distillation.py:72-77 pins prior/decoder in_features. In the trainer motion_ids appears only at scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:232 (`routed_ids = motion_teacher_ids[motion_command.motion_ids]`, feeding route_teacher_actions for the label) and 644 (`eval_motion_ids = ...clone()`, used only for per-clip reporting at 683-691). Student calls are mu_prior(proprio, zwin, cmd) and act(proprio, z_cmd); snmr/integration/distillation.py:65-97 shows prior_input concatenates at most [proprio, cmd, z_proj(zwin)] and act() concatenates only (proprio, z_cmd).
findings.consequence: C1 exclusivity is enforced by constructor arithmetic, not convention — a stray argument cannot be added without changing in_features and failing the test. Safe to assert in the paper.

findings.claim: Stronger than the test covers: in E70 the privileged critic_obs never reaches the student at all, because E52_DET=1 disables the posterior.
findings.evidence: scripts/run_e70_multitraj.sh:180 sets E52_DET=1; train_e52_dagger.py:110 reads it. In the training loop (443-450) `if deterministic: mu_res = torch.zeros_like(mu_p); mu_q = mu_p; mu_z = mu_p` — student.mu_residual is never called. At eval, eval_z defaults to 'prior' (line 563) and E70 never sets E52_EVAL_Z, so the posterior branch at 662-663 never executes. `priv` is computed at 276-277 and discarded.
findings.consequence: Removes a whole class of leak worry: critic_obs contains motion_ref_pos_b, robot_body_pos_b, base_lin_vel and other privileged reference terms, and none of them touch any E70 student. Worth one explicit sentence, since CommandStudent advertises a posterior a reader will assume was used.

findings.claim: One real but bounded training-time channel: the `actions` term inside PROPRIO is the last EXECUTED action, which during DAgger is a teacher/student mix, and teacher actions are routed by motion_id. It is absent at evaluation.
findings.evidence: holosoma's actions term returns env.action_manager.action (managers/observation/terms/wbt.py:109-118). Training executes `actions = mix * a_teacher + (1 - mix) * a_student` at scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:401-402, with p_teacher annealing to floor 0.1 (run_e70_multitraj.sh:181). The evaluation loop (671-674) steps only student.act output — no teacher mixing.
findings.verdict: PARTIAL — a real training-time path, empirically bounded and inert at measurement time
findings.consequence: Does not threaten the result: (a) the measured quantity is an evaluation rollout in which no teacher acts, so the trace is gone at measurement; (b) whatever identity is recoverable from proprioception alone is bounded by b_prior_proprio, which sees exactly this and nothing else and scores 0.4365 ambiguity / 0.4307 general — the floor, not the effect. Shared identically by all five arms. A limitations footnote at most.

findings.claim: Evaluation reset states are identical across arms by construction, and reset noise is explicitly nullified, so the arms share bit-identical physical initial conditions.
findings.evidence: snmr/integration/wbt_bodyfix.py:85-131 — the patched MotionCommand.reset calls holosoma's orig_reset (which applies NoiseToInitialPoseConfig noise, config_values/wbt/g1/command.py:7-15, overall_noise_scale=1.0) and then, when evaluating with a frozen start grid, overwrites sim.dof_pos/dof_vel/robot_root_states with the exact reference state; the comment at 113-115 states the intent. train_e52_dagger.py:640-643 sets the grid and asserts `torch.equal(motion_command.time_steps, starts)` or raises.
findings.consequence: Fully discharged for the evaluation; the realized grid is verified, not assumed. freeze_at_timestep_zero_prob defaults to 0.0 (config_types/command.py:130) and is never set in the g1 WBT config, so it is inert, as is start_at_timestep_zero_prob. All arms run --training.seed 404 for every eval mode (run_e70_multitraj.sh:135-157).

findings.claim: Training-time phase sampling is adaptive and therefore NOT identical across arms — but the adaptation direction is self-correcting and cannot manufacture the effect.
findings.evidence: config_values/wbt/g1/command.py:36 sets use_adaptive_timesteps_sampler=True; managers/command/terms/wbt.py:601-608 updates failed-phase bins from terminated episodes and resamples from them, so each arm's realized start distribution tracks its own failure pattern.
findings.verdict: PARTIAL — identical sampler configuration, non-identical realized distribution
findings.consequence: Disclosed upstream (BeyondMimic) behavior on a shared config, and the bias runs against the headline: a weaker arm gets MORE training on the phases it fails, compressing arm differences rather than inflating them. Since the SNMR arm claims the advantage, an equalizing curriculum makes +0.191 conservative. One sentence; not a threat.

findings.claim: Ambiguity starts are identical across arms, content-hashed, and their clip ordering is asserted at load.
findings.evidence: run_e70_multitraj.sh:37 pins PRECHECK_HASH and line 41 gates on it before anything runs; every ambiguity eval passes the same E52_EVAL_STARTS_JSON. train_e52_dagger.py:600-628 rejects the file unless pair_report['clips'] == clip_names and exactly two motions are loaded, and rejects any window lacking a full 500-step horizon. The precheck carries 69 windows and an explicit `side_transform: swap first/second for loader lexical order`, so the source-screen ordering mismatch is handled rather than silently absorbed.
findings.consequence: Identical across arms and tamper-evident. Note for interpretation: the precheck's state_proxy is 'previous_dof_target + root_angular_velocity + dof_pos + dof_vel' — exactly the actor's PROPRIO slice — so ambiguity is defined in the student's own proprioceptive coordinates, which is the right construction.

findings.claim: The clock null is genuinely identity-free, and a latent fragility that could have broken it did not fire because the two E70 clips are exactly the same length.
findings.evidence: snmr/integration/distillation.py:253-293 uses one shared frequency bank and one fixed seed-63 projection indexed by LOCAL frame. Verified bit-identical at equal local indices on the real E70 pool (local idx 0 and 5000 both exactly equal across clips) and between-clip mean separation exactly 0.000. Both frozen motions are 13066 frames (walk1_subject1_mj_z.npz, walk1_subject5_mj_z.npz, latent_z shape (13066,128)).
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED, with a latent fragility to flag
findings.consequence: Two attacks are closed: (a) with unequal clip lengths, local indices past the shorter clip's end would occur only in the longer clip, making the tail identity-revealing by exclusion — equal lengths make this vacuous; (b) `periods = logspace(1, log10(max(max_length,20)), 16)` depends on the max clip length in the LOADED pool, so a clock student trained on two clips but evaluated through the single-motion eval_only branch (train_e52_dagger.py:190-206) would silently get a different frequency bank than it was trained with. E70 always loads both clips, so it never fired; it should be pinned with an assertion before the clock arm is reused.

findings.claim: Concern 4's premise is correct — the destroyed code did carry proprio-derived features — but the mechanism is narrower: raw proprioception still reaches the decoder, so proprioceptive INFORMATION is not removed.
findings.evidence: snmr/integration/distillation.py:65-76 — prior_input concatenates proprio with cmd and/or z_proj(z_window), so z_cmd = f(proprio, goal) in every arm. But line 63 builds `decoder = mlp([proprio_dim + z_cmd_dim, ...])` and lines 96-97 make act() return `decoder(cat(proprio, z_cmd))`. destroy_command_code (312-326) takes only the (envs, dim) code and never touches proprio. Verified by construction: decoder in_features = 154 = 90 + 64 in every arm.
findings.verdict: PARTIAL — premise correct, mechanism narrower than stated
findings.consequence: The right statement is that destruction removes the encoder's learned nonlinear summary of proprioception, not proprioception itself; the decoder still has the raw state and simply was never trained to act on state alone. This matters for wording: 'destroying the command also blinds the policy to its own body' would be wrong.

findings.claim: 'Every bit of competence flows through it' conflates a structural fact that needs no experiment with a behavioral claim the experiment does not support.
findings.evidence: Structural half: distillation.py:63 and 96-97 prove goal, retargeting latent, clock and motion ID can reach the action ONLY via z_cmd (C1), pinned by tests/test_distillation.py:72-77 and instantiated at train_e52_dagger.py:255-263. Behavioral half: all frozen results are exactly 0.000 completion — explicit seed0 zero/shuffle/marginal_random (e70/students/seed0_explicit/c_prior_explicit_eval_destroy_*.json) and all nine E75 SNMR cells (e75_snmr_destruction/students/seed{0,1,2}_snmr/, survival 0.54-0.84 s, teacher_action_rmse 0.91-1.40). All three modes are off the code manifold: `zero` is outside the distribution; `marginal_random` (distillation.py:322-325) matches per-dim marginals but destroys joint AND temporal correlation, redrawn every 50 Hz tick; `shuffle` (roll by 1 across the env batch) delivers a valid code from an env at a different clip, phase, and physical state — off-manifold conditional on the current state.
findings.verdict: PARTIAL — structural claim defensible without the experiment; behavioral claim over-stated
findings.consequence: Recommended wording: 'every bit of GOAL information flows through z_cmd' (architecture, provable) plus 'the decoder has no proprioception-only fallback: all three code interventions collapse completion to zero' (measurement). Drop 'competence'. The experiment does not decompose z_cmd into goal content versus state-coupled content, and the advisor is right that it cannot.

findings.claim: E77's already-frozen dose-response is the strongest existing evidence FOR the advisor's reading, and it is already in hand.
findings.evidence: /data/robotixx/snmr-research/e77_degradation_pilot/. Explicit arm zero-order hold: k=1 0.9258, k=2 (0.04 s) 0.8623, k=5 (0.1 s) 0.2227, k=10 0.0000, k=20 0.0000. SNMR arm: 0.6982 / 0.5664 / 0.0039 / 0.0000 / 0.0000. Noise titration graded too (explicit sigma 0.5 -> 0.8447, 1.0 -> 0.3926, 2.0 -> 0.0000). Implemented at scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:566-580 and 655-667.
findings.consequence: A channel carrying only slow motion semantics should tolerate a 0.1 s hold — a walking reference barely moves in 100 ms — yet the explicit student falls to 0.223 and the SNMR student to 0.004. Direct measured evidence that the channel carries fast state-coupled content, i.e. the advisor's hypothesis. It also reframes E75 helpfully: 0.000 is the endpoint of a continuous dose-response curve, a stronger and more honest claim than a binary knockout.

findings.claim: The shuffled arm carried EXACTLY as much linearly-decodable clip identity as the winning SNMR arm, and it bought nothing — this upgrades the lead's observation from qualitative to quantitative.
findings.evidence: Measured on the frozen E70 latents: between-clip mean separation after per-arm standardization is 8.042 std units in 128-d for the SNMR latent and 8.042 for the shuffled latent (the cyclic swap at snmr/integration/distillation.py:242-249 relabels the two clusters, preserving both), versus exactly 0.000 for the clock. Pooled three-seed ambiguity completion (/data/robotixx/snmr-research/e70/analysis_seed0-1-2.json): explicit 0.9733, snmr 0.7542, time 0.5622, shuffled 0.5524, proprio 0.4365; snmr_minus_time +0.1908 [0.1239, 0.2741].
findings.consequence: The strongest available form of the argument: an arm whose command channel is identity-separable to precisely the same degree as the arm that wins by +0.199 scored 0.5524 — indistinguishable from the identity-free clock's 0.5622 and only +0.116 over the identity-free, phase-free proprio floor. If clip-ID+phase lookup were the mechanism, this arm had everything it needed. Report with the quantitative framing, not just 'identity was recoverable in principle'.

findings.claim: It remains weak evidence, for a reason worth stating rather than hiding.
findings.evidence: same_phase_shuffled_latents (distillation.py:220-250) supplies identity as 128-d encoded cluster membership that must be inverted through a fixed permutation, and nothing in the action-matching objective (train_e52_dagger.py:461) rewards learning 'when I see clip B's code, emit clip A's action.' docs/E70_SHUFFLE_CONTROL_AUDIT_2026-09-10.md section 4 already says this.
findings.consequence: Absence of inversion under an objective that never asked for inversion is not evidence that a directly-supervised clip-ID+phase student would fail. The shuffled arm bounds accidental exploitation, not the capability. Keep the audit doc's framing — a measurement, not a guarantee — and do not use it as a substitute for the missing arm.

findings.claim: A proper clip-ID + phase arm requires new training code. The E71 infrastructure does not and cannot supply it.
findings.evidence: scripts/eval_e71_command_swap.py is a frozen-STUDENT counterfactual evaluator: ARM_GOALS at 108-111 admits only c_prior_explicit and a_prior_snmr; line 1163 raises on any student with time_index or shuffle_latent set; EXPECTED_STUDENT_SHA256 at 101-107 pins all six E70 checkpoints; build_four_cell_grid (snmr/integration/counterfactual_eval.py:376-421) builds state x command cells from existing commands. It was never run: no outputs anywhere under /data/robotixx/snmr-research, no reproducibility/reports/*e71*, and docs/E71_COMMAND_SWAP_PROTOCOL.md:5 says 'no simulator run; not preregistered' with the freeze manifest 'pending; not instantiated' (line 333). Searching snmr/ and scripts/ finds no clip-identity code builder for the command channel; the only synthetic builder is shared_time_index_latents.
findings.consequence: The needed arm is small and well-scoped: a sibling of shared_time_index_latents emitting [one-hot clip id || existing sinusoidal local-phase features] at width Z_SNMR_DIM, one new E52_* flag beside phase_only/shuffle_latent at train_e52_dagger.py:236-249, and a unit test asserting equal-local-index codes differ ONLY in the identity block. It then rides the identical z_window/_latent_at_offsets path, so lookahead matching to the latent, clock and shuffled arms is automatic. Cost is one training run per seed — not the cheap eval-only job E71 was. E71 stays worth running for its own question (does the student follow a valid swapped command from the same state), which is the clean decomposition concern 4 actually needs.

findings.claim: Capacity is not the explanation for the explicit arm's win — the explicit and SNMR arms have identical prior input width and identical prior parameter counts, and the SNMR arm has strictly MORE live parameters.
findings.evidence: Instantiating CommandStudent(90, *, 29, goal, 64, z_window_dim=256, z_cmd_dim=64): explicit and snmr both give prior_in=154, decoder_in=154, prior_params=227136; z_proj adds 82240 parameters that are LIVE only in the snmr/explicit+snmr arms (distillation.py:53, 72-76) and dead in the explicit arm. The proprio arm alone differs (prior_in=90).
findings.consequence: Pre-empts the 'the explicit arm just had a better-conditioned or bigger network' review. The representation arms carry an extra 82k-parameter projection the explicit arm never uses, so any capacity asymmetry runs against the explicit arm, not for it.

actions: Do not change any E70 conclusion on the strength of concerns 1, 2, or 3. Normalization is matched-in-form and capacity-neutral; the observation normalizers are literally shared objects; evaluation resets are exact-state and seed-matched with a realized-grid assertion. State this in the methods rather than leaving it to be asked.

Soften the E75/destruction wording. Replace 'every bit of competence flows through the command channel' with two separable claims: (a) structural — the decoder's inputs are exactly [proprio(90), z_cmd(64)], so all goal, latent, clock and motion-ID information reaches the action only via z_cmd (distillation.py:63, 96-97; tests/test_distillation.py:72-77); (b) behavioral — all three code interventions collapse completion to 0.000 on both the explicit and SNMR arms, so the decoder has no proprioception-only fallback. Explicitly note that raw proprioception still reaches the decoder, so the interventions do not blind the policy to its own state.

Promote E77 from pilot to reported result alongside E75. The hold-k curve (explicit 0.926 -> 0.862 at 0.04 s -> 0.223 at 0.1 s -> 0.000 at 0.2 s) is the graded version of the knockout and is direct evidence the channel carries fast state-coupled content rather than only slow motion semantics. It concedes the advisor's point from a position of strength and pre-empts the 'binary knockout proves nothing' review.

Upgrade docs/E70_SHUFFLE_CONTROL_AUDIT_2026-09-10.md section 4 to the quantitative form: between-clip mean separation after standardization is 8.042 std units for BOTH the SNMR and shuffled codes and exactly 0.000 for the clock. 'Identity was recoverable in principle' becomes 'identity was separable to precisely the same degree as in the winning arm, and bought nothing.' Keep the existing caveat that this is a measurement, not a guarantee.

Add an assertion pinning the clock arm's frequency bank. shared_time_index_latents derives `periods` from the max clip length in the LOADED pool (snmr/integration/distillation.py:276-282), so a clock student trained on two clips and evaluated through the single-motion eval_only branch (scripts/train_e52_dagger.py:190-206) would silently receive a different code than it was trained with. E70 never triggers this — both clips are 13066 frames and both are always loaded — but it should be checked rather than relied on.

Build the clip-ID + phase arm as a new TRAINING arm, not as an E71 mode: a `clip_id_phase_latents(starts, ends, output_dim)` builder emitting [one-hot clip id || existing local-phase sinusoids], a fourth mutually-exclusive E52_* flag beside phase_only/shuffle_latent, and a unit test that equal-local-index codes differ only in the identity block. It inherits the z_window/_latent_at_offsets path, so lookahead matching is automatic. Budget one training run per seed.

Keep E71 on the queue for what it uniquely answers — the same-state valid-command swap is the only built instrument that separates 'the channel is load-bearing' from 'the channel's content is the goal,' which is the decomposition concern 4 asks for and E75 cannot provide. Its freeze manifest is still uninstantiated (docs/E71_COMMAND_SWAP_PROTOCOL.md:333).

Add one limitations sentence acknowledging that the explicit arm's own 58-d reference (joint_pos + joint_vel at the current frame) is a near-unique (clip, frame) fingerprint on deterministic clips, so the explicit-vs-latent gap is not itself free of the memorization reading. This is the honest version of concern 5 applied to the control arm, and stating it costs nothing.

Note that the training-time phase sampler is adaptive per arm (use_adaptive_timesteps_sampler=True) and that its bias direction is equalizing — failing arms get more practice on the phases they fail — so the +0.191 snmr-minus-time contrast is conservative with respect to it. One sentence.

No re-runs are required by this audit. The eval-nondeterminism question a reviewer would raise next is already answered by E76 (about 18% of individual rollout outcomes flip on re-run under identical inputs, while the arm-level contrast agrees to 0.003, docs/E76_EVALUATION_REPLICATION.md) — cite it rather than re-deriving it.
